summary: Holistic test audit across Tasks 1-8 for agent-native-distribution. Test suite is green: 645 Rust tests + 27 vitest = 672 passing, 0 failures, 4 ignored (all with documented rationale). AC1-AC17 plus the Error Catalogue rows each map to at least one test that exercises the production code path. The HMAC confirmation gate, public-write ceremony, soft-fall router, install symlink hardening, and doctor's six checks are all driven by production triggers (FailingEmbedder, port-0 ECONNREFUSED trick, real symlink fixtures, malformed tarball, expired token files, fetch stubs returning 503) — none of the negative-path tests are hand-crafted response stubs. Concurrent-consume race uses tokio::Barrier with 16 tasks. Pyramid balance is healthy for an L feature: ~25 unit + ~50 integration + 0 true E2E (with AC3 netns deferred as documented). Findings: (1) AC3 unshare -rn netns isolation test does not exist — currently covered by integration-style assertions on outbound-call absence rather than a real network namespace. Documented as a known gap that T12 manual QA picks up via airplane mode. (2) Byte-for-byte manifest snapshot only checked for `mnemonik-attest.md`; other six manifests checked only via Purpose:/Trigger: substring presence. (3) `resolve_visibility` / `resolve_allow_fallback` have no dedicated #[test] units; integration coverage in sign_memory_visibility.rs is comprehensive but the resolvers' pure-function nature would benefit from a few cheap inline unit tests. None of these block merge. T12 (pre-deploy QA) inherits the AC3 manual smoke and the byte-for-byte snapshot gap as items to verify against the freshly-built binary.

A real netns test on Linux-only CI would be a strong follow-up; not a v1 blocker since v1 is macOS-only and `unshare` is Linux-only.

findings.title: No `unshare -rn` netns isolation test for AC3 offline cold-start
findings.description: The tech-spec calls for an E2E test that runs `mnemonic-mcp mcp-stdio` inside `unshare -rn` (Linux network namespace with only `lo`) and asserts (a) sign_memory succeeds, (b) `ss -tn state established` returns zero non-loopback connections, (c) `strace -e trace=connect` records zero non-loopback connect() calls. No such test exists in the suite. The current AC3 defense is indirect: hosted endpoint pointed at an unreachable URL, env-var-disabled pricing refresh, and code-path inspection showing local-mode sign_memory does not invoke the hosted client.
findings.recommendation: Defer to v1.1 (Linux CI follow-up) or add a `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`-gated test that spawns `unshare -rn` as a child process. T12 pre-deploy QA should explicitly run airplane-mode smoke per user-spec §Как проверить row 7 to compensate. Document the gap in T12's report so it doesn't become invisible after merge.

findings.title: Byte-for-byte manifest snapshot only covers 1 of 7 manifests
findings.description: The byte-for-byte equality assertion against `skills::ALL_SKILLS` exists only for `mnemonik-attest.md`. The other six manifests (help, init, recall, checkpoint, verify, status) are only validated via `Purpose:` / `Trigger:` substring presence in tools_list_enriched_with_purpose_trigger. A subtle build-time projection bug that corrupted the body of, e.g., `mnemonik-recall.md` could pass the substring check.
findings.recommendation: Loop over all 7 names in resources_read_returns_full_markdown_for_attest (rename to `resources_read_returns_full_markdown_for_each_manifest`) and assert byte-equality for each via `resources/read`. Tiny addition (~10 lines).

findings.title: Three error catalogue rows lack production-trigger integration tests
findings.description: OAuthTimeout (-32096), LocalStorageBusy (-32099), and IdentityBootstrapFailed (-32094) have their wire shapes pinned at the helper level (one `assert_eq!` per row) but no integration test triggers them via the production code path. Tech-spec line 353 names `hung_oauth_mock`, `held_sqlite_lock`, and a mock-KeyStore fixture respectively. The wire contract is protected (a refactor dropping `data.expires_at` from OAuthTimeout would still fail the helper test), but the actual surfacing path is unverified.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable for v1 — these are existing/external error codes the feature plumbs through; HostedUnavailable + TokenExpired DO get full production triggers via sign_memory_softfall. Track for v1.1 as test depth improvement. T12 should ensure these helpers don't get repurposed without follow-up coverage.

findings.title: No dedicated unit tests for resolve_visibility / resolve_allow_fallback
findings.description: `resolve_write_mode` has a dense unit-test suite (12 cases at tools.rs:2105+); `resolve_visibility` and `resolve_allow_fallback` (its newer siblings) have only integration coverage via sign_memory_visibility.rs. The integration coverage is thorough — local+public (presence-only), local+private (presence-only), participate+5-case-variants, non-bool allow_fallback — so functional coverage is fine, but pure-function unit tests at the resolver level would catch a regression faster than an integration failure deep in the dispatcher stack.
findings.recommendation: Add ~6 unit tests inline in tools.rs `mod tests` mirroring the resolve_write_mode shape: None defaults; explicit Public/Private under participate; presence-rejection under local; non-string rejection; case-variant rejection. Not blocking.

findings.title: `stdio_backward_compat::test_stdio_tools_list_sign_memory_recall_without_oauth` could drop #[ignore]
findings.description: The test is ignored with rationale 'pricing.refresh() needs internet'. Task 5 added `PRICING_REFRESH_DISABLED=1` to skip the network call (see `mcp_stdio_accepts_jsonrpc_on_stdin`); the same env var could unblock this older test.
findings.recommendation: Either drop #[ignore] and add `.env(PRICING_REFRESH_DISABLED=1)` to the spawn, or delete the test if mcp_stdio_accepts_jsonrpc_on_stdin fully supersedes it. Not blocking.

findings.title: AC15 mismatch-warning stderr line not asserted
findings.description: AC15 requires not only that `initialize` surfaces `embedder.model_id` + `model_version` + `dim` (covered) but also that on connect, `mnemonik-mcp` compares its compile-time values against the hosted peer's reply and emits a stderr warning line `[mnemonik-mcp] embedder version mismatch: local=<x> remote=<y>, cross-mode recall not guaranteed consistent` on mismatch. Tech-spec line 359 lists this as the second E2E. No such test exists. The mcp-stdio binary today does discovery locally per Decision 1 (binary-embedded manifests), so the only scenario where mismatch could surface is during participate-mode proxy, which doesn't have an `initialize` round-trip to compare.
findings.recommendation: Either implement the mismatch-warning emission path (currently absent from the binary's behaviour as best I can tell) and add the test, or update the user-spec to drop the mismatch-line requirement on the grounds that local-only discovery makes the divergence unobservable in v1. T12 should flag this for the spec disposition.
